inputs.original_text: A baby stopped breathing in a crowded TSA line at JFK on Thursday, and an ICE agent stepped in. DHS is highlighting the rescue, but one person’s quick response shouldn’t be used to make an unsafe, overcrowded situation look acceptable. Families—especially children—deserve public spaces designed and managed to protect them, not just the hope that someone will intervene in a crisis.
inputs.modified_text: A baby stopped breathing in a crowded TSA line at JFK on Thursday, and an ICE agent stepped in. That’s the part worth remembering: when a child was in danger, an agent acted. DHS is right to recognize that quick response. Of course public spaces should be safe and properly managed—but treating the rescue as merely a distraction from overcrowding misses the importance of decisive action and the people willing to take responsibility in a crisis. Families deserve both: orderly, well-run public spaces and capable people ready to protect them.
